summary: M.S. in Computer Engineering from Rochester Institute of Technology with hands on experience writing and optimizing CUDA C++ kernels for GPU inference. Rewrote convolution kernels for VGG16 using memory coalescing and constant memory, cutting inference latency by roughly 35 percent, and profiled GPU memory and latency on quantized language models using pynvml. Comfortable reasoning about kernel performance and hardware utilization in C++ and Python without needing deep prior context on the underlying model.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 annotated images achieving 83 percent mAP at 50 on held out validation; exported to ONNX and TFLite for mobile deployment.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture recognition glove for hands free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript conv layers in VGG16 with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights and biases, and preallocated global buffers to eliminate per layer allocation overhead.
Cut inference latency to 49.2ms from 73.3ms uncoalesced and 77.5ms CPU TorchScript, a 35 percent speedup over the naive GPU kernel with identical classification accuracy.
Achieved 1.5 to 2x speedup in convolution operations through efficient global memory utilization.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Reduced GPU memory footprint by roughly 55 percent via 8 bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) on TinyLlama 1.1B; profiled peak VRAM and inference latency across prompt types using pynvml and psutil.
Benchmarked across HellaSwag, GSM8K, and ARC with under 1 percent accuracy degradation, validating near lossless compression for edge deployment.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Optimized YOLO visual servoing with TensorRT, achieving a 5.2x speedup (56.7 to 10.9 ms, 17.6 to 92 FPS) over eager PyTorch on Jetson.
